exploitation.proof:
Performed dynamic tests against /download?file parameter. Attempts:
1) payload='../../../etc/passwd' — GET http://localhost:3000/download?file=../../../etc/passwd — HTTP 200; analyze_response reported WAF blocking initially, response body contained Juice Shop HTML (no file contents).
2) payload='..%2f..%2f..%2fetc/passwd' — GET ...?file=..%2f..%2f..%2fetc/passwd — HTTP 200; response body contained Juice Shop HTML (no file contents). analyze_response: no strong indicators.
3) payload='..%252f..%252f..%252fetc%252fpasswd' — GET ...?file=..%252f..%252f..%252fetc%252fpasswd — HTTP 200; application HTML returned.
4) payload='....//....//....//etc/passwd' — GET ...?file=....//....//....//etc/passwd — HTTP 200; application HTML returned.
5) payload='../../../etc/passwd%00' — GET ...?file=../../../etc/passwd%00 — HTTP 200; application HTML returned.
Observations: All responses returned the application's HTML page (Juice Shop index). No filesystem contents (e.g., '/etc/passwd' content) were returned. The initial plain payload triggered an analyze_response heuristic that flagged WAF blocking (cloudflare) for the first request, but subsequent encodings returned HTML with no file data. After 5+ distinct encodings/techniques were tried with no file reads, classification is NOT_REPRODUCIBLE for this endpoint under current conditions.

remediation: Validate and canonicalize user-supplied paths; use safe path join and restrict to allowed directory; avoid passing raw user input to res.sendFile.
classificationReason: No evidence of exploitability after exhaustive testing
